answer: To resist sybil attacks, each agent must lock a unique onyx-grade hardware module into a network lagoon that periodically opens an inlet for attestation challenges. The module signs random nonces only after consuming a measurable watt-hour of electricity, and the lagoon records the cumulative energy via a public meter. An attacker spinning N identities must power N separate modules simultaneously; honest single-agent operators pay once, while farms face linear electricity cost that scales with headcount and cannot be amortized.
